findings.source_quote: τινὲς δὲ τραχεῖς καὶ μὴ συμφωνοῦντες τοῖς ἑτέροις λίθοις
findings.issue: The lexical metadata attributes the cut/fit distinction to λατομεῖν and ἁρμόζειν, but ἁρμόζειν does not occur in this selected section. The expression translated “out of keeping with” is μὴ συμφωνοῦντες. This misidentifies the source wording underlying the English.
findings.suggested_revision: Revise the lexical entry to distinguish the λατομέω forms used for cutting from συμφωνοῦντες used for agreement or compatibility with the other stones. Remove ἁρμόζειν from this section's source-word attribution, or explicitly identify it as a cross-section reference rather than wording present here.

findings.source_quote: ἐκέλευσε οὖν πάντας τούτους ἐκ τοῦ πύργου μετενεχθῆναι καὶ τεθῆναι παρὰ τὸν πύργον, καὶ ἑτέρους ἐνεχθῆναι λίθους καὶ ἐμβληθῆναι εἰς τὸν τόπον αὐτῶν.
findings.english_quote: Retain the master’s authority, the shepherd’s responsibility and the distinct fates of the stone categories.
findings.issue: The theological metadata claims that this section retains the shepherd's responsibility, although the selected section neither identifies the shepherd as an actor nor assigns him responsibility. This imports content from outside the reviewed unit into its account of what the translation preserves.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove the claim about the shepherd's responsibility from this unit's metadata. Describe the inspecting man's commands and the different treatment of the stones, or explicitly label any broader contextual discussion as outside this section.

findings.source_quote: καὶ ὅταν ἐπάτασσεν, ἐγένοντο αὐτῶν τινὲς μέλανες ὡσεὶ ἀσβόλη, τινὲς δὲ ἐψωριακότες, τινὲς δὲ σχισμὰς ἔχοντες, τινὲς δὲ κολοβοί
findings.english_quote: When he struck them, some became black as soot. Some were scabby, cracked or chipped.
findings.issue: The Greek's ἐγένοντο governs the successive stone conditions: these conditions emerge when he strikes the stones. Splitting the account into “became” for black stones and “were” for the remaining conditions loses that change-of-state force for the latter categories.
findings.suggested_revision: Keep the change-of-state wording governing all seven categories, for example by beginning “When he struck them, some became black as soot; others became scabby, cracked, or chipped …” and reviewing the continuation against the remaining Greek clauses.

findings.source_quote: τινὲς δὲ τραχεῖς καὶ μὴ συμφωνοῦντες τοῖς ἑτέροις λίθοις
findings.issue: The simplified edition's lexical metadata independently misattributes its cut/fit distinction to ἁρμόζειν, which is absent from this selected section. “Did not fit with the other stones” renders μὴ συμφωνοῦντες, not ἁρμόζειν.
findings.suggested_revision: Identify συμφωνοῦντες as the source expression for compatibility with the other stones and the λατομέω forms as the source for cutting. Remove or clearly label the out-of-section reference to ἁρμόζειν.

findings.source_quote: ἐκέλευσε οὖν πάντας τούτους ἐκ τοῦ πύργου μετενεχθῆναι καὶ τεθῆναι παρὰ τὸν πύργον, καὶ ἑτέρους ἐνεχθῆναι λίθους καὶ ἐμβληθῆναι εἰς τὸν τόπον αὐτῶν.
findings.english_quote: Retain the master’s authority, the shepherd’s responsibility and the distinct fates of the stone categories.
findings.issue: This unit's theological metadata introduces the shepherd's responsibility, which is not narrated or assigned in the selected section.
findings.suggested_revision: Limit this unit's description to the inspecting man's authority and the narrated treatment of the stones. Remove the shepherd-responsibility claim or explicitly distinguish it as broader context.

findings.source_quote: Καὶ ἰδοὺ μετὰ μικρὸν βλέπω παράταξιν πολλῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐρχομένων
findings.english_quote: Retain all seven stone conditions, the three strikes, the two-day interval, inside/outside placement, setting aside versus rejection and no-joint selection; preserve all substantive alternative notes.
findings.issue: The simplification metadata claims to retain a two-day interval and a no-joint selection, neither of which occurs in this selected section or its English text. The section's opening interval is merely “after a little while.” These are inaccurate unit-level preservation claims, not evidence of omissions that should be filled from other sections.
findings.suggested_revision: Remove the two-day-interval and no-joint claims from this unit's simplification metadata. Retain only distinctions actually present here; do not add the absent material to the translation.

findings.source_quote: καὶ οἱ ἓξ ἄνδρες οἱ εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν | ἐπιτάξαντες, ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ ἀριστερῶν μετ᾿ αὐτοῦ περιεπάτουν. καὶ πάντες οἱ εἰς τὴν οἰκοδομὴν | ἐργασάμενοι μετ᾿ αὐτοῦ ἦσαν
findings.english_quote: The long span from “directed” through “on the building” includes a bar-marked supplement in the1891 working Greek
findings.issue: The simplified note copies an English endpoint from the standard edition: “on the building” does not occur in the simplified text. Consequently, its quoted locator does not accurately identify the supplement's extent for this edition's readers.
findings.suggested_revision: Use a locator that exists in the simplified edition, or describe the supplement directly: it includes the directing clause, the right-and-left accompaniment, and the reference to all the building workers, ending before the Greek word for “worked.” Preserve the distinction between reconstructed Greek and reported surviving Athos wording.

summary: Both editions require revision, principally to correct unit-specific metadata; the simplified text also loses the change-of-state force governing the stone conditions. The standard main text covers the selected clauses faithfully. Retaining “three times” is compatible with the disclosed bounded working selection, and the supplied reports support the count note's stated alternatives without establishing fresh manuscript verification. The editorial supplements should remain distinguished from preserved witness text. This review assesses the supplied source and reports only; proposed corrections require fresh review.
